title: Trust Comparison Tool
learning_objectives: Evaluate when trusts are cost-effective versus unnecessary
Compare different trust types for specific family situations
Calculate probate costs versus trust setup and maintenance costs
Understand that trusts aren't only for wealthy families
description: Interactive tool for analyzing four family situations to determine if a trust is appropriate, which type of trust fits best, and whether the cost-benefit analysis supports trust creation.
instructions: Analyze four distinct family situations with varying complexity and assets
Calculate estimated probate costs if no trust
Compare trust setup and maintenance costs to probate savings
Recommend specific trust type (if any) for each situation
Identify life triggers that should prompt trust creation

situations.name: Young Couple with Life Insurance and Small Children

details.current_planning: No will, no trust, no beneficiary updates since children born

probate_avoidance_value.details: Life insurance avoids probate via beneficiary designation, but retirement/savings don't

control_need.details: Cannot name children directly as life insurance beneficiaries—minors can't own assets. Without trust, court appoints custodian until age 18, then lump sum to teenager.

complexity.details: Straightforward family structure but minor children require protected management

trust_options.description: Trust created in will, activates upon death, holds life insurance proceeds
trust_options.benefits: Protects children from receiving lump sum at 18; professional management; controlled distribution (e.g., 1/3 at 25, 1/3 at 30, 1/3 at 35)

trust_options.description: Holds all assets now, avoids probate entirely
trust_options.benefits: Probate avoidance on all assets, privacy, immediate distribution, professional management for children

analysis.recommendation: Testamentary trust MINIMUM (necessary for children); revocable living trust if want to avoid probate on all assets
analysis.cost_benefit: Testamentary trust: $800 setup prevents lump sum to minors and provides oversight. Revocable trust: $3K setup saves $15K probate.
analysis.urgency: CRITICAL—parents of minor children need this immediately

details.name: Jennifer
details.wishes: Parents cared for during their lives, then remainder to environmental charity

probate_avoidance_value.details: Estate over $850K; probate costs in {{STATE_NAME}} typically 3-7% of estate value

control_need.details: Sequential distribution (parents first, then charity) possible through will but trust provides more control

privacy_value.details: Professional reputation/privacy concerns; probate is public record

trust_options.description: Holds all assets, avoids probate, provides privacy
trust_options.benefits: Probate savings $36,500; privacy; immediate distribution; no court involvement

analysis.recommendation: Revocable Living Trust—probate cost savings ($36,500) far exceed setup expense ($3,000)
analysis.cost_benefit: Setup $3K + 10 years maintenance $3K = $6K total vs. probate $42.5K = $36.5K NET SAVINGS

children.david: Two children from first marriage, ages 20 and 22
children.maria: One child from first marriage, age 17

details.wishes: Provide for current spouse during lifetime, but ensure assets ultimately go to own children

complexity.details: Competing interests between current spouse and children from prior marriages

control_need.details: Simple will leaving everything to spouse provides no guarantee children receive anything. Spouse could remarry, change will, or disinherit stepchildren.

without_trust_risk.scenario: David dies first, leaves all to Maria
without_trust_risk.outcome: Maria inherits everything, no legal obligation to David's children. If Maria remarries or changes will, David's children get nothing.
without_trust_risk.family_impact: Guaranteed conflict, potential litigation, damaged relationships

trust_options.risk: Cannot achieve both goals (spouse support + children inherit). Spouse receives all with no guarantee to children.

cost.future_litigation_risk: High—children may sue claiming undue influence

trust_options.description: Spouse receives income for life; principal to children at spouse's death
trust_options.benefits: Achieves both goals; legally binding; prevents spouse from disinheriting children; professional administration

trust_options.type: Marital Trust with Separate Trusts for Children
trust_options.description: Portion to marital trust (spouse income), remainder directly to trusts for own children
trust_options.benefits: Maximum control; guaranteed distributions; flexibility in timing

analysis.recommendation: QTIP or similar marital trust—ONLY way to achieve both goals (spouse support + children inherit)
analysis.cost_benefit: $5,000-6,000 setup prevents family warfare, litigation ($50K+), and ensures wishes honored. Priceless for family harmony.
analysis.urgency: CRITICAL—blended families without trusts almost always result in conflict

control_need.details: Straightforward situation, no dependents, no special circumstances

complexity.details: No special needs beneficiaries, no complex family dynamics

trust_options.analysis: Trust setup ($3,000) completely unjustified for $45K estate. Probate cost ($2K) less than trust setup.

analysis.recommendation: NO TRUST NEEDED—simple will sufficient. Priority: Healthcare directive and POA more important than will at this stage.
analysis.cost_benefit: Trust would cost $3,000 to save $2,000 probate—makes no financial sense
analysis.urgency: Low for will; HIGH for healthcare directive and financial POA
analysis.what_changes: Consider trust when: (1) Have children, (2) Assets > $500K, (3) Receive large inheritance, (4) Complex family situation emerges

analysis_questions.question: What surprised you about who needs trusts?
Is estate size or family complexity more important in determining trust need?
analysis_questions.sample_answer: Family complexity often matters more—young parents with modest assets need trusts for children; single person with $1M might not need one if straightforward

analysis_questions.question: Calculate the net savings for Situation 2 (Jennifer) of creating a trust:
Why is Situation 3 (blended family) CRITICAL for trust even beyond financial savings?
analysis_questions.sample_answer: Only way to achieve both goals (spouse support + children inherit). Prevents family warfare, litigation, and ensures wishes honored. Family harmony value exceeds financial cost.

analysis_questions.question: What life events should trigger trust consideration?

key_takeaways: Trusts aren't only for the wealthy—young parents with life insurance often need them most
Blended families almost always need trusts to avoid conflict and achieve dual goals
Probate costs 3-7% of estate value; trust setup costs $1,500-$5,000 depending on complexity
Testamentary trusts (in will) provide control without probate avoidance; revocable trusts do both
For small, simple estates, trusts aren't cost-effective—simple will suffices
In {{STATE_NAME}}, probate costs and procedures vary by county but typically follow state guidelines
